title: How banks work
examples: If I put money in the bank, do I get it back?
How does the bank make a profit from my money?
What is the difference between a deposit and a loan?

explain.say: Today we will learn how banks work in our economy.
First, let us look at deposits. A deposit is when you give your money to the bank.

draw.text: Deposits: Giving money to the bank

explain.say: The bank keeps your money safe so you can use it later. This keeps your money secure.

draw.text: Deposits: Kept safe by the bank

explain.say: Next, we look at loans. A loan is when the bank lends money to someone else.

draw.text: Loans: Bank lends money to people

explain.say: When you take a loan, you promise to pay the money back later. This is a repayment plan.
Finally, we discuss interest. Interest is the extra payment for using the bank's money.

faq.q: How does the bank actually make money from this process?
faq.a: The bank makes money by charging interest on the loans they give out. They also sometimes charge fees for services.
asks: Where does the bank's profit come from?
Is interest the only way banks earn money?

faq.q: If I deposit money, will I earn interest too?
faq.a: Some banks pay interest on deposits, but this is not always the case. It depends on the bank's current rates.
asks: Do I get paid for keeping my money there?
Is there interest on savings accounts?

faq.q: What is the difference between a loan and a deposit?
faq.a: A deposit is money you give to the bank, and a loan is money the bank gives to you.
asks: Am I giving or receiving money?
Which way is the money moving?

faq.q: Does the bank use my deposited money to give out loans?
faq.a: Yes, banks use a portion of the deposited money to give out loans to others. This is how the money circulates.
asks: Does the bank mix up my money?
How does the bank keep the money moving?

faq.a: The interest rate is the percentage that shows how much extra money you must pay back. It is usually shown as a percentage.
asks: How do I calculate the interest?

facts: Banks act as middlemen between people who have money and people who need money.
When you deposit money, the bank holds it securely for you.
A loan requires the borrower to pay back the original amount plus interest.
Interest is the cost of borrowing money, usually expressed as a percentage.

quiz.say: Sarah deposits ten pounds into her bank account. This action is called:
quiz.why: A deposit is when you give money to the bank to keep safe.

wrong.0: Interest is the extra payment, not the initial action.
wrong.1: Withdrawal is taking money out, not putting it in.
wrong.3: A loan means you are receiving money from the bank.

quiz.say: If a bank lends one hundred pounds and charges ten pounds in interest, what is the total repayment?
quiz.why: The total repayment is the original loan amount plus the extra interest paid.

wrong.0: This only counts the interest and forgets the original loan.
wrong.1: This incorrectly suggests no interest was charged.
wrong.3: This forgets to add the extra cost of borrowing.

quiz.say: A person needs money to buy a new bicycle. The bank gives them money, and they promise to pay it back over time. This process is best described as:
quiz.why: When you receive money with a promise to repay it, it is a loan.

wrong.0: Interest is only the extra cost, not the main transaction.
wrong.1: Savings is just keeping money aside, not borrowing it.
wrong.3: A deposit is when you give money to the bank.
